page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-128 is a compute-optimized instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 64 physical AMD EPYC 7B13 cores with simultaneous multithreading, providing 2.0 threads per core. The system is configured with 128 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and PassMark CPU physics tests all scoring in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks also reaches the top 10%, while large block read and write bandwidths fall into the top 25%. In cryptographic workloads, the instance achieves top-tier results, aided by hardware-accelerated AES and VAES instruction sets. Single-core performance is generally strong to average, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scoring in the middle 50%, while multi-threaded ray tracing ranks in the top 10%.

The hardware profile presents a clear tradeoff: while raw multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth are highly performant, the low memory-to-vCPU ratio limits its suitability for memory-intensive databases or large-scale in-memory processing. For instance, LLM inference on a large 70B model results in weak text generation speeds in the bottom 25%. However, the high density of dedicated AMD EPYC cores makes this instance highly cost-efficient for compute-bound workloads. It is well-suited for software compilation, ray tracing, static web serving, and parallelized CPU-bound tasks.
